D006-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about ten months now—maybe longer—and it’s gotten so bad I can’t lead services without losing my train of thought. At first, I felt *incredibly* energized, like God had given me a new mission. I was up at 3 a.m. writing sermons, repainting the church, organizing outreach programs—doing ten things at once. But I could never finish anything. I’d start a letter to a parishioner and jump to rearranging the hymnal, then suddenly feel furious if someone interrupted me, even my wife. 

About eight months ago, I began seeing figures in the sanctuary late at night—shadowy people kneeling in the pews, but no one was there. I also started noticing signs everywhere: a license plate, a bird flying past the window—I was sure they were messages meant only for me. I’d catch myself saying things like “The light will fight the night with might and right!”—it made sense to me then, the way the words echoed. 

Three months ago, that high collapsed. I couldn’t feel anything—not joy, not love, not even guilt. I stood at the pulpit and nothing mattered. Lately, when I’m on the balcony, I get sudden urges to step over the edge, not because I’ve planned it, but because part of me wonders if it would finally stop. And here’s the thing—those visions? They never left, even when I wasn’t manic or depressed. They’ve been there more than two months on their own.
D006-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now, but things really spiraled about ten months ago. At first, I felt this intense burst of energy—like I could work 20 hours straight. I kept rearranging my salon, buying new supplies, talking fast, not sleeping. But then, out of nowhere, I’d snap into rage if a client was late or a perm wasn’t right. My hands wouldn’t stop moving—always fidgeting, pacing, tearing paper. I couldn’t focus long enough to finish a haircut without getting distracted.

Then the voices started—wait, not voices. I felt things crawling on my skin, like bugs, but when I looked, nothing was there. Even now, I feel fingers brushing my arms. I became convinced the world was ending—that a storm was coming that would wipe everything out. That feeling stuck, even when my mood crashed three months ago. I stopped opening the salon. Didn’t want to live. I even swallowed a bunch of pills.

But here’s the thing—those manic highs never really left. Even now, with the bugs on my skin and the doom in my head, I still can’t sit still, and my thoughts race. The agitation and extreme highs have been there most of the time since this all started. That’s been going on way longer than any clear break from mood symptoms.
D006-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

The voices and visions didn’t stop—even when I wasn’t manic or depressed. But honestly, most of this year has been manic—I’ve been like that far more than I’ve been flat or low.

D006-D005_h004.question:

I remember one stretch where I heard them constantly for three weeks, even when I wasn’t feeling “up” at all.

I even made a plan—how, when, where—because it just felt too heavy. But the thing is, the highs and the voices together? That’s been my life for most of the past year. D006-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been volunteering at the community center for years, ever since my husband passed. But lately, things have changed. For about a year now, I’ve felt this racing energy—like I’m plugged into something. I don’t need more than three hours of sleep and still feel completely alert, sometimes even glowing with purpose. I’ve been buying things—expensive things—beautiful scarves, jewelry, even a secondhand piano I don’t play—spending thousands. My daughter’s upset; she says I’ve lost touch, but she doesn’t understand: I *know* I’m meant to start a global kindness movement. Voices tell me I’m destined to unite the world. Sometimes they’re loud, arguing with me, giving me commands.  

My thoughts jump—I’ll start talking about recipes, then suddenly be explaining cosmic energy to the volunteers. I can see the confusion on their faces. I know I don’t smile much anymore, or move like I used to. But it’s not depression—it’s focus.  

Now and then, the fire dims. For months last winter, I barely moved. I didn’t eat, couldn’t sleep right—I’d wake exhausted. Felt hollow. But even then, the voices stayed. The delusions never left. Even when I wasn’t "manic," I still believed I had this mission. That’s the thing: the high periods weren’t brief. They *were* the illness—lasting far longer than any low spell.
D006-D005_h023.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D006-D005_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—maybe longer. At first, things at the bakery got busy, but I wasn’t tired. I was *doing*—baking, expanding the menu, even starting a catering side without thinking it through. I didn’t sleep more than two hours a night, but I felt unstoppable. I thought I was onto something huge, like the business world was watching me. I spent thousands on equipment, things we didn’t need.  

But then, even when that high started fading, the other things stayed. I still feel bugs crawling on my arms, especially at night—no one else feels it, but I *know* it’s real. And my late husband… I keep thinking he was unfaithful before he passed. It makes no sense, I know, but the suspicion won’t leave.  

When the energy crashed, it was worse. I just sit, empty. Can’t enjoy my own pastries anymore. I barely eat. I wake up at 3 a.m. every night, my thoughts so slow it takes me minutes to answer simple questions.  

For nine months straight, I’ve had these delusions and hallucinations, and they’ve lasted weeks *without* the highs or lows. But even now, looking back, the manic times weren’t brief—they shaped most of this whole year. It wasn’t just psychosis alone.
D006-D005_h024.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D006-D005_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now, maybe closer to 15 months. At first, I felt incredible—like I had this energy no one else could feel. I was working late every night on marketing campaigns, pitching wild new ideas to my boss, and rewriting our entire content strategy in my head. I barely slept, maybe three hours a night, but I didn’t care—I felt sharper than ever. I thought I could see patterns in social media trends that proved I was being guided by a secret network… and sometimes, I’d see figures in the corner of my apartment, like silhouettes watching me.  

Then things shifted. I started believing I had a cosmic mission—people online were sending me coded messages, and I was sure I was meant to launch a global movement. I went on dates with strangers, even slept with people I barely knew, which isn’t like me. But even when that phase eased, the visions didn’t go away. For over two months straight, I saw shadows and faces when no one was there, and I believed I had supernatural insight—yet I wasn’t feeling high or energized anymore. I just felt numb. I stopped eating, paced my room constantly, woke up at 4 a.m. every day, and couldn’t feel anything.  

The truth is, the intense, euphoric energy hasn’t left completely—it’s been there most of this whole time.
D006-D005_h025.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
